title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)
description: UN General Assembly Resolution 217A of 10 December 1948: 30 articles proclaiming the common standard of rights for all peoples.

title: United States — Bill of Rights (1791)
description: The first ten amendments to the U.S. Constitution, ratified 15 December 1791: speech, arms, due process, and the reserved-powers rule.

title: European Convention on Human Rights (1950)
description: The Council of Europe's 1950 convention, in force 1953, with the Strasbourg court that lets individuals petition across borders.

title: Magna Carta (1215)
description: The Great Charter of 15 June 1215 at Runnymede: clauses 39 and 40 planting the seed of due process and the rule of law.

title: France — Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen (1789)
t: France — Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen (1789)
description: Adopted 26 August 1789: 17 articles proclaiming liberty, legal equality, and the sovereignty of the nation.

title: South Africa — Bill of Rights (1996)
description: Chapter 2 of South Africa's 1996 Constitution: 35 sections including justiciable socio-economic rights.

title: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (1966)
t: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (1966)
description: The binding 1966 treaty, in force 1976, with the Human Rights Committee and individual-complaint protocol.

title: Canada — Charter of Rights and Freedoms (1982)
t: Canada — Charter of Rights and Freedoms (1982)
description: Part I of Canada's Constitution Act 1982: fundamental freedoms, democratic, mobility, legal, and equality rights with section 1 limits.
